findings.title: Earpiece hints queued on the couch are marked as seen at once; when a death, disconnect or server stop on the couch drops the queue, the hint is never shown, now or later.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/npc/Hints.java:77-80 (s.mark before Emcee.deliver); the drops are in src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/show/Interviews.java:84-91 (DISCONNECT/DIED), 95-96 (reset -> Emcee.clearHeld on SERVER_STOPPED) and 316-323 (finish sends to the disconnecting player)
findings.what_happens: A crawler's first interview usually comes on the way from depth 1 to 2, which is also their first descent. During it, EarpieceHints queues the place-rule hint ('rule'), the next-tick 'sponsor' hint and the 'green_room' hint of the entry room, each marked seen at once. If the player drops connection, the server stops or crashes, or they die on the couch (the floor clock runs during the interview), those hints are discarded. Hints show 'once per player, ever', so this player never hears how a place's rule works or that sponsors are calling. The unlock toasts that were waiting are lost the same way, and they never reach the client's 'Just unlocked' list (ShowClient.unlocked fills it only from UnlockPayload). On a disconnect, finish() pushes the waiting lines to a connection that is already closed, and RunFlow.onJoin sends nothing again on the same floor.
findings.evidence: Game test CouchReviewGameTests.aHintHeldOnTheCouchIsNotLostForGood: invite, accept, DESCENDED 1->2, then RunEvents.DIED. It fails with "the earpiece's rule hint is marked seen but was dropped with 5 waiting things on the couch; Hints.show again: false". aHintHeldOnTheCouchSurvivesAStop (ShowFlow.reset(), which SERVER_STOPPED calls) fails with "the rule hint is marked seen and dropped with 5 waiting things". Before this commit Hints.show sent the payload at the descent, so the hint was heard.

findings.title: The floor clock's warnings (10/5/1 minutes left, the countdown banner) for the floor the crawler is sitting on now wait for the end of the interview.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/show/ShowFlow.java:392-400 (onAirtime -> Emcee.announce -> say/banner -> Emcee.deliver); the hold is started at ShowFlow.java:112-114
findings.what_happens: The interview does not pause the floor clock (RunFlow.tickFloor keeps running). Airtime comes back only if the crawler opened the floor (Interviews.finish, s.fresh). Example: crawler B's teammate opened depth N+1 long ago, and B arrives for an interview of up to 8 minutes (120 s per page). B's 'one minute left' line and banner with its jingle, and the red COUNTDOWN banner, are all held. Before this commit they showed and played over the dimmed interview screen, which does not pause the game, so B could walk off. Now B hears nothing until the set strike kills them on the couch, and the DIED listener then throws the warnings away. If the interview ends first, a stale 'ten minutes left' is read after the floor card while the HUD clock shows less.
findings.evidence: Game test CouchReviewGameTests.theClockWarningDoesNotWaitOnTheCouch: a crawler on the couch on floor 2, then RunEvents.AIRTIME for floor 2 with 60 and then 10 seconds left. It fails with "one minute and ten seconds left on the crawler's floor: 4 warnings (lines and banners) wait for the end of the interview". The action-bar count for 9..1 seconds (ShowFlow.java:404) still bypasses the hold, so the crawler gets digits without the warning lines.

Nothing needs a decision to close a finding. Things worth knowing:
(a) Finding 6, design question for the owner: the couch time of the crawler who opened a floor is still given back to that floor when the interview ends, so the mates' clock visibly jumps up at that moment. Pausing the floor clock during that crawler's couch would avoid the jump, but it changes the airtime design, so I left it.

findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/mob/CrawlMonster.java:842 (die -> Abilities.onDeath) and Abilities.java:632-640; clip at tools/content/mob/understage_anim.py, the bunny's 'death'; picture /home/user/shots/CREATURES1B/strips/dust_bunny_death.png, frames t1-t6
findings.what_happens: When a dust bunny is killed, two bunnies at 0.7 scale fly out of it at once, with a POOF of 12 particles, while the parent still stands whole. For the next half second the player sees three bunnies. Then the parent bulges and shrinks to nothing on its own, so the pinch and the pop no longer cause anything. In the strip, full bunnies leap past the intact parent at t1 to t4 under a cloud of white particles, and the pinch is hidden.
findings.evidence: CrawlMonster.die calls Abilities.onDeath on the first death tick, and the SPLIT branch spawns both copies with an upward kick right there. The clip pinches at 0.24-0.42 s and pops at 0.6 s. Deaths.dust_bunny puts its ash at tick 6 and its pop at tick 11, so the copies come about 11 ticks before the moment the clip shows them being made. strips/dust_bunny_death.png shows it.

findings.title: Several loop clips sample a fast wave with too few keys, so the motion they describe comes out flat: the Rat King's whiskers and jaw, the understudy's wringing hands, the bunny's tuft and its stun squash
findings.where: tools/content/mob/understage_anim.py:423 (ratking idle, 8 keys, whiskers/jaw use s(p*4)), :209 (hopeful idle, 8 keys, hand_r/hand_l/forearm use s(p*4)), :121 (bunny idle, 8 keys, tuft s(p*4)), :166 (bunny stun, 4 keys, body* s(p*2)); written to crawl_anims/ratking.json, hopeful.json, bunny.json
findings.what_happens: The Rat King's idle promises 'whiskers working' and a jaw that chews, but both stay still. The understudy's idle promises 'hands wrung', but its hands and forearms hold one fixed angle for the whole 3 s loop. The bunny's tuft ('a nose that never stops') never moves, and its stun does not squash. These creatures stand stiffer than their clips claim.
findings.evidence: loop() keys f at i/n. Sampling sin(2*pi*4p) at p=k/8, or sin(2*pi*2p) at p=k/4, always gives sin(k*pi) = 0. In the written JSON, every key is exactly zero on ratking idle whiskers/jaw, hopeful idle hand_r/hand_l, bunny idle tuft and bunny stun body scale. Hopeful idle forearm_r/forearm_l are constant at -55 in every key. I found this with a check over crawl_anims/*.json for tracks whose keys never change.

findings.title: As a black shape, the heckler is nearly the rat wrangler's double: same height, same capped flat head, same square body; only a small bag tells them apart
findings.where: /home/user/shots/CREATURES1B/silhouettes_understage.png, row 2 (rat_wrangler 3/4 vs heckler 3/4); the plan 'heckler' in tools/content/mob/understage.py:104
findings.what_happens: At ten blocks a player cannot tell the heckler (a ranged thrower who stays back) from the rat wrangler (a melee pusher who sends rats). Both read as the same stocky capped man.
findings.evidence: I aligned the black shapes at their feet. heckler vs rat_wrangler (3/4 view) overlap with IoU 0.79, the highest pair involving any 1B kind. Next come heckler vs prompter at 0.69 and rat_king vs grandmother at 0.69. Heights are 185 vs 179 px and widths 104 vs 95 px. Both have the same cap brim. The heckler's only distinct mark is the bag at hand height.

findings.title: The heckler's thumbs-down habit spins the hand a full turn back to rest in its last 0.02 s, so one rendered frame shows the fist twisted sideways
findings.where: tools/content/mob/understage_anim.py:320-326 (habit.thumb: key 1.78 hand_r yaw 360, then key 1.8 {})
findings.what_happens: At the end of each thumbs-down, the right fist flicks for one frame at 60 fps before the clip fades out.
findings.evidence: Sampling the built clip at 60 fps (anim.sample) gives hand_r a 33 deg jump at t=1.783 and a 327 deg jump at t=1.8. The 360-to-0 rule ('a whole turn is no turn') applies only to keys held after a clip ends, not to a key inside it.

findings.where: /home/user/shots/CREATURES1B/sw/ (empty); strips/understudy_*.png; fight/ (only fight1b_rat_king_b_06/_12 and fight1b_grandmother_lint_b_06/_12)

result.checked: I rebased lane-b onto origin/claude/determined-edison-xwiksi and read the diffs of all seven commits. I followed them into Animator, AnimClip, AnimSet, MonsterRenderer, PlanModel, HelperRenderer, CrawlMonster (wind-up, scene, tickDeath, freeze), Abilities (passive, use, dash, onDeath), Blows, Deaths, Director (elites), the understage roster and understage_anim.py, and checked the particle code in /home/user/ref/mcsrc. tools/dev/jc.sh passes. I wrote three scratch harnesses under /tmp/rv1b/src (FrozenDeath, FrozenAttack, FrozenStale). They run the real Animator on the shipped hopeful.json clips against the jc.sh classes. I ran tools/dev/balance.sh at depths 5 and 9 for both bosses: Rat King 186 % / 168 %, Grandmother Lint 224 % / 242 %, all inside the 150–250 % boss band, so no balance finding (log in /tmp/rv1b/balance.log). I looked at the engineer's fight pictures, forty_1b.png and the rat_king_run strip at full size. Things I checked that hold: the heavy blows' 12-tick contact matches the 0.6 s clip contact and mob_blows.py; the death lengths equal the clips (60/60/26/12/32/30); title (50 ticks), act and enrage clips fit their motion lengths; the Rat King's act-two 360-degree turn fades out without spinning back (held value); a frozen monster's delayed hit is refused (hitNow -> doHurtTarget checks FROZEN); the dash fix keeps the direction; no summoned helper, armour set or screen uses the new plans; no new allocation per frame. The client cost number (50.0 -> 50.1 ms per tick) I could not reproduce or disprove. I did not run mp.sh, load.sh or a client run: the build lock was held by another lane's full test run for most of the session.

findings.title: The heckler's tomato and Grandmother Lint's lint ball are already flying when the throw animation starts: the server launches the shot on the same tick as the clip, but the clips release it 0.4 s (8 ticks) later.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/mob/Abilities.java:237-247 (RANGED spawns the MobShot inside use()) and :195-201 (the ability clip starts the same tick); tools/content/mob/understage_anim.py:345-356 (heckler ability.ranged: wind-up 0.22-0.32 s, release at 0.40 s, tomato still in the hand until 0.45 s) and :624-628 (granny: lob at 0.40 s)
findings.what_happens: A tomato thrown at 1.1 blocks per tick from 3-8 blocks away hits the crawler before the heckler's arm comes over. For the first 0.45 s the heckler still holds a second tomato behind his head while the real one splats on the player. The tell comes after the damage. The same order shows on the summons: the Rat King's rats and Grandmother Lint's dust bunnies are already standing there before the first sceptre bang (0.30 s) or her call (0.30-0.95 s).
findings.evidence: Code path: Abilities.tick -> use(RANGED) runs shot.shoot and level.addFreshEntity, then Abilities.java:201 starts Motion.ABILITY 'ranged' in the same server tick. Clip data in crawl_anims/heckler.json and granny.json (from understage_anim.py): arm at the top at 0.22-0.32 s, release key 'in' at 0.40 s, 'tomato*' (-1,-1,-1) only from 0.45 s. SUMMON (Abilities.java:266-281) spawns the helpers inside use(); ratking ability.summon keys its bangs at 0.30, 0.58 and 0.86 s.

findings.title: An understudy that is watched in the middle of its grab finishes the grab before it strikes its star pose: freezing does not end the attack clip.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/mob/Abilities.java:48-56 (FROZEN is set, the motion is left running); src/client/java/net/kasax/crawl/client/mob/anim/Animator.java (holds are applied before the action clip, which is OVER and wins)
findings.what_happens: The understudy attacks from behind and the player turns round. Instead of snapping into the star pose ('watched, it snaps into a star pose and holds it'), it keeps clapping its arms shut on the player for about half a second. It reaches the star pose only about 0.7 s after it froze. The hit itself is cancelled, but the picture says it struck.
findings.evidence: Scratch harness /tmp/rv1b/src/net/kasax/crawl/client/mob/anim/FrozenAttack.java runs the shipped hopeful.json: grab started at t=1.00 s, frozen from t=1.10 s. arm_r stays in the clap (roll 4-6 deg, pitch -77 to -92) until t=1.40 s and reaches the star pose (roll 130 deg) only at t=1.80 s. The attack motion lasts contact+12 = 15 ticks (CrawlMonster.startHit). passive() sets only the flag, never breakAction() or a motion change.

findings.title: An understudy killed or stunned while it is watched snaps its head by the whole held look turn 0.25 s into its death; the star pose also stays on the parts its death does not move.
findings.where: src/client/java/net/kasax/crawl/client/mob/anim/Animator.java:315-333 (the frozen branch uses st.lookYaw unscaled by lookW, and the whole look block is skipped once lookW reaches 0); CrawlMonster.java:466 (passive(), which clears FROZEN, runs only while alive)
findings.what_happens: A melee player always looks at the understudy when killing it, so it is frozen at death. During the overplayed death its head keeps the frozen turn, then jumps back in one frame when the look weight runs out. pose.frozen also stays held under the death clip, so forearm_l, hand_l and the hips' rotation stay in the star pose while it bows. A stun spell cast on a watched understudy causes the same head snap.
findings.evidence: Scratch harness FrozenDeath.java (hopeful.json, head turned 40 deg, frozen from 1 s, killed at 2 s with HOLD_FROZEN still set): 'head yaw 28.0 -> 0.0 deg in one frame' at t=2.250 s (deathTime 5, lookW 0). lookTarget is 0 when deathTime > 0 or on STUN (line 315), but yawL = st.lookYaw ignores lookW. The death clip's last key does not name forearm_l, hand_l or hips (understage_anim.py:259-277).

findings.title: In multiplayer, a client that turns towards an understudy someone else has frozen shows its head held at an old angle from the last time that client drew it.
findings.where: src/client/java/net/kasax/crawl/client/mob/anim/Animator.java:320-325 (the frozen head reads st.lookYaw unless the state is fresh; a culled monster keeps a stale AnimState)
findings.what_happens: Player A watches the understudy and freezes it. Player B, who last saw it seconds ago while it looked the other way, turns round and sees its head turned the wrong way. The head stays that way for as long as it is frozen and snaps when A looks away. The two clients disagree on where the creature is looking.
findings.evidence: Scratch harness FrozenStale.java: the client draws it for 1 s with the server head turn +50 deg, stops drawing it for 8 s, then draws it frozen with the server head turn -20 deg. It shows head yaw 35.0 deg for the whole frozen time instead of following -20. MonsterRenderer reuses m.clientAnim across culling, so fresh is false; Animator.update is only called for drawn entities.

findings.title: Elite cable gnawers show nothing when they use their elite ability: the new plan has no ability clip and no 'cast' fallback, and the old cast swing it replaced is gone.
findings.where: src/main/modules/mob/assets/crawloffame/crawl_anims/gnawer.json (no ability.*, cast, enrage or pose.* clips); Animator.java:220 (falls back to 'cast', otherwise nothing); PlanModel.setupAnim returns before the old swings for any plan with clips; Director.java:163 and :212-220 (regulars become elite 4-16 % of the time; understage.json: stage_rats regular = cable_gnawer)
findings.what_happens: An elite gnawer that leaps, charges, enrages, shields, clouds, steals or calls for help stands in its idle or run cycle with no tell: the 16-tick charge wind-up is a motionless rat that then shoots forward. Under the old 'rodent' plan the cast swing (head down, jaw open) and the charge lean showed it. The elite heckler falls back to 'cast', but it has no pose.enraged, pose.shield or pose.charge either. docs/CREATURES.md: every ability is a clip of its own, with 'cast' as the fallback.
findings.evidence: Clip lists read from the shipped JSON: gnawer [] (no ability or cast clip); heckler ['ability.ranged', 'cast']. Ability.ELITE_POOL = LEAP, CHARGE, EXPLODE, STEAL, ENRAGE, SHIELD, CALL_HELP, CLOUD. Abilities.java:201 sends Motion.ABILITY <ability>; Animator finds neither 'ability.<id>' nor 'cast' and starts nothing. The old look was "plan": "rodent" (git show fd20ee4^:.../crawl_looks/cable_gnawer.json), whose fourLegs() moved head and jaw on s.cast.

findings.title: The dust bunny's split happens before its 'pinches in two' death: both halves pop out at full size on the first tick, and the halves later die the same split death with nothing coming out.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/mob/Abilities.java:632-641 (SPLIT spawns in onDeath at tick 0, no Motion.SPAWN); understage_anim.py:168-174 (death 0.6 s: bulge 0.12 s, pinch 0.24-0.42 s, pop at 0.6 s)
findings.what_happens: Three bunnies are on screen for 0.6 s: the two new ones are already hopping away from a POOF while the parent only starts to bulge and pinch, so the kind's idea ('hit it, get two') reads backwards. The halves never play their own spawn clip (it exists: 'spawn', squash-in from 0.3 scale). When a half dies it plays the same pinching-in-two death, and nothing appears.
findings.evidence: Director.spawnNear(..., true) in onDeath runs in die() before tickDeath plays the 12-tick clip. Only SUMMON sends s.motion(Motion.SPAWN) (Abilities.java:281). Deaths 'dust_bunny' plays WHITE_ASH at t=6 and POOF at t=11, after the children are already out. Split children are the same kind with split=true, so the same death clip plays.

findings.title: The Rat King's death scene says the rent 'comes down from the grid as crumbs', but the crumbs hang in mid-air and drift slightly upwards.
findings.where: src/main/java/net/kasax/crawl/mob/Deaths.java:180-187
findings.what_happens: From t=38 to t=58, specks appear 4-5 blocks above the stage and fade where they are, rising a little. Nothing falls, so the arena's reaction reads as floating dust, not crumbs raining down.
findings.evidence: sendParticles(DustParticleOptions, ..., count 1, dx 0, dy -0.1, dz 0, speed 0): with count > 0 the offsets are only a position spread and the velocity is 0. In mcsrc, Particle(level,x,y,z,xa,ya,za) adds a random direction and +0.1 to yd; DustParticleBase multiplies the velocity by 0.1 and has no gravity (Particle.gravity defaults to 0). The result is an upward drift of about 0.004-0.016 blocks per tick. Grandmother Lint's WHITE_ASH does fall (ash has its own gravity), so only the Rat King's scene is affected.
